method.agent: scripted oracle: always issues a correct call or script; measures cost and information loss, not model behaviour
method.tokens: input = tokens read by the model across all turns without prompt caching (schemas + prompt + every earlier call and result); context = schemas + calls + results counted once
method.effective: effective input (a model, not a measurement) = the static prefix (prompt + tool schemas) is written to the cache on the first turn at 1.25× and read at 0.1× on every later turn, while everything the conversation added since (calls and results) is billed at 1×; conservative because earlier turns are not assumed cached either
method.turns: model turns including the closing answer turn; parallel calls in one turn count once
method.latency: tool ms = wall-clock of all tool traffic per round, median with min–max (fresh server process each round, so cold start is included for every strategy); no model involved. A 95th percentile is only shown from 20 samples on, otherwise the maximum
method.modeled: modeled ms = tool ms (median) + assumed model time: turns × 1500 ms + input tokens ÷ 1000 × 20 ms (raw input); the turn-time sweep repeats it for 500 / 1500 / 3000 ms per turn. These are assumptions to explore sensitivity, not measurements
method.lookups: cold: discover_tools, then describe_tool, then call (2 extra turns; the agent ignores the inline signatures). merged: discover_tools returns the signature of the best-matching tool(s) and the agent calls straight away (1 extra turn; a describe_tool turn is added only when a needed signature is missing). known: the agent already knows the server and the signatures (0 extra turns). The main tables use `cold`; the cold-start section compares all three
method.pinned: pinned: lazygate with expose = [get_order_status, list_tickets, get_ticket, get_region_metric] merged into tools/list (their schemas are in context every turn, no lookup turns); every other tool goes through discover_tools, describe_tool and call_tool
method.directCap: direct_capped: like direct, but a client that truncates MCP output at 25,000 tokens cuts larger tool results (the oracle then works with the truncated text); direct is the uncapped upper bound
method.schemas: filler tool schemas use the built-in 3-property template (see the measured tokens per tool next to each catalog); use --schema-tokens-per-tool or --catalog-from to size them from a real catalog
method.discoveryCost: exp. turns / exp. ms add the held-out wrong-tool rate × 1 retry turn(s) for every run that used discover_tools (a modeled penalty: a wrong top result costs the agent another discovery turn); the oracle itself never gets it wrong
method.catalog: direct puts every tool schema in context; lazygate strategies list only the meta-tools (pinned adds a few tools) and pay discover_tools / describe_tool turns
